about: Line numbers and highlighted lines of code blocks, as written in the note. `before` is a note with one code block; `options` are set on it; `after` is the note then. The TypeScript tests check the editor writes exactly `after` (and reads the options back); the Rust tests check every Typst `after` is valid Typst.

typst.name: line numbers are turned on
typst.after:
#[
#show raw.line: it => [#box(width: 2em, text(fill: luma(150), str(it.number)))#it.body]
```python
a = 1
b = 2
c = 3
d = 4
```
]

typst.name: a line is highlighted
typst.after:
#[
#show raw.line: it => if it.number in (2,) [#highlight(fill: rgb("#fff3bf"), it.body)] else [#it.body]
```python
a = 1
b = 2
c = 3
d = 4
```
]

typst.name: a few lines are highlighted
typst.after:
#[
#show raw.line: it => if it.number in (1, 3) [#highlight(fill: rgb("#fff3bf"), it.body)] else [#it.body]
```python
a = 1
b = 2
c = 3
d = 4
```
]

typst.name: a run of lines is written as a range
typst.after:
#[
#show raw.line: it => if it.number in (..range(1, 4)) [#highlight(fill: rgb("#fff3bf"), it.body)] else [#it.body]
```python
a = 1
b = 2
c = 3
d = 4
```
]

typst.name: line numbers and highlighted lines together
typst.after:
#[
#show raw.line: it => [#box(width: 2em, text(fill: luma(150), str(it.number)))#if it.number in (..range(2, 5)) [#highlight(fill: rgb("#fff3bf"), it.body)] else [#it.body]]
```python
a = 1
b = 2
c = 3
d = 4
```
]
